findings.evidence: previous-version digest jira at dbff837f: 'removed units (351, showing 40)'. All 40 shown items are explained by record.md rows or sections.json units. The other 311 could not be checked from the digest.
findings.fix: Regenerate the dbff837f digest without the cut, or check the 311 unshown units against docs/audit/recovery/jira/record.md and sections.json. Add a row for any unit that no section-id row covers.

findings.evidence: 'Show the exact change: original versus new text, the exact command or tool call, and side effects' and 'Get approval for that exact change' are generic approval steps a capable model mostly applies already.
findings.fix: Keep the Jira-specific reasons (watchers notified, one-way transitions, no undo, displayed payloads were not executed). Tighten the generic show-and-approve wording to one clause. Remove nothing without a record row.

findings.evidence: '**Story or task:** creating one or rewriting its description, also read references/story-anatomy.md ... For a draft card, the reply opens with the three bold As a / I want / so that lines ... Sprint: the next future sprint, never the active one ... Do not load story-anatomy.md for bugs...' puts loading rules, an output template and a sprint policy in one paragraph.
findings.fix: Split the paragraph into three short bullets: (1) when to load story-anatomy.md and when not to, (2) the draft-card opening format, (3) the sprint default. That keeps the Process pattern readable without moving content out of SKILL.md.

findings.evidence: 'Sprint: the next future sprint, never the active one'. references/story-anatomy.md rule 6 says 'Never the active sprint unless the user explicitly asks', so SKILL.md drops the escape hatch.
findings.fix: Sprint: the next future sprint by default, never the active one unless the user explicitly asks (adding scope changes a running sprint's commitment); state that reason and write the chosen sprint id into the command.

findings.evidence: Some queries read like spec phrasing, not user messages: 'Design a Jira workflow policy in prose without accessing an instance', 'Implement a fix from a pasted bug report without looking up or changing any Jira issue'. 'Create GitHub issue #42 for the failing test' is an easy negative.
findings.fix: Rewrite these as realistic near-misses with casual wording and context, for example: 'my PM pasted the bug from PROJ-55 below, just patch checkout.ts, dont touch jira'. Keep the 10/10 split.

findings.evidence: 'REST GET /rest/api/3/search/jql (Cloud; the old /search is being removed)' is a version-sensitive endpoint fact with no source URL or check date. The DC half of the same line carries a date.
findings.fix: Add the official source and the date checked, for example '(Cloud, VERIFIED in the v3 OpenAPI spec, developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/, checked <date>)', or tell the agent to confirm the endpoint live.

findings.evidence: Step 1 is one sentence with nested parentheses: transitions, a multi-hop route from a trusted workflow graph, getJiraWorkflows disabled by default, the CLI-only REST listing and required create fields. The transition branch is hard to follow at a glance.
findings.fix: Split step 1 into sub-bullets: edit (fetch the issue), move (list transitions; if the target is missing, one approved hop at a time; CLI-only setups use REST per mcp.md Transitions row), create (required fields from createmeta). Keep every clause.

findings.evidence: previous-version digest at dbff837f: "removed units (93, showing 40)". All 40 shown items have valid record rows (not-lost, intended-change, generic-model-knowledge drops, or user-accepted drops), but 53 removed units were not shown and could not be checked
findings.fix: Regenerate the digest with the full unit list (or judge against docs/audit/recovery/lesson-learned/sections.json in full) so every removed unit, including s014's lost 'Also worth noting' compact format, is checked against a row in docs/audit/recovery/lesson-learned/record.md

findings.evidence: "Rank them by observable consequence and evidence strength; a demonstrated trade-off beats a neat principle match." The removed 'lead with what works' rule is not replaced, so nothing says how to choose between a well-evidenced win and a well-evidenced introduced cost when both are candidates
findings.fix: Add one tie-break clause to step 2, e.g. "when a win and an introduced cost are equally evidenced, lead with the one the user's next change is most likely to repeat", which keeps the reflective purpose without restoring the dropped tone rules

findings.evidence: "Not for generic engineering tutorials, ordinary bug reviews, or implementing refactors." The near-misses in the skill's own trigger set (commit messages, release notes, postmortems, squashing history) are not named as boundaries, and the WHAT does not mention untracked files or pasted logs
findings.fix: Use when users ask what they learned, want an engineering takeaway, or reflect on recent commits, a branch diff, a specific commit, staged/unstaged or untracked changes, or a pasted git log, even without naming Git or a principle. Reads the changes and grounds one lesson in concrete code or test evidence, with a next-time practice. Not for generic engineering tutorials, bug reviews, refactor plans, commit messages, release notes or incident postmortems.

findings.evidence: Six evals cover casual, written, rename, range, untracked and no-change cases, but none tests the merge-commit gotcha (empty combined diff), the two-dot vs three-dot branch diff, or base-branch detection when origin/HEAD is missing
findings.fix: Add one eval with an evals/files/ fixture of a clean merge commit (git show output empty, --first-parent output non-empty), with assertions that the answer does not report 'no changes' and cites the first-parent diff

findings.evidence: Working changes row: "`git diff`, `git diff --cached`, and every `??` path from `git status`". `git status --short` collapses an untracked directory into one `?? dir/` line, so following this branch on a new untracked folder gives a directory path and not the new files in it
findings.fix: Change the row to "... and every `??` path from `git status --short --untracked-files=all` (the default collapses a new directory into one `?? dir/` line)", and add that fact to ## Git gotchas

findings.evidence: "On the base branch, a dirty tree means working changes first..." The skill never says how to tell whether HEAD is on the base branch, a feature branch or detached (e.g. checked out at a tag or in a rebase), so the default-scope branch has to be guessed
findings.fix: Add before the table: "Get the current branch with `git branch --show-current`; empty output means detached HEAD: treat it like the base-branch case (working changes, else last 5 commits) and say so."
